description: Add a character to the encounter in progress, on a side. Player characters default to the party and NPCs to the foes. The turn order keeps each side together in the order the rule set's initiative set; when a side-initiative order is already settled, a late joiner joins their side's block. A character who is not at the encounter's location is still added, and the result carries a warning to act on. An NPC with no attacks is also warned about: give them attacks with update_npc before their turn if they are meant to fight.

Put a participant on a cell of the encounter map, counted from 0 at the top left: column increases to the right and row increases downward. Moving is limited to the rule set's movement per turn, counted in cells moved in a straight line or diagonal. Obstacles block: a cell with a blocking object cannot be entered or be the destination, so the participant goes around it. Terrain that costs extra movement to enter takes that many moves for each cell entered. That limit applies only to the participant whose turn it is; moving anyone else is free, though they still cannot enter a blocked cell. The first placement is free. Use this to move a participant, not to tell the story of how they got there.

force.description: Allow the move even though it costs more than the movement left this turn, onto a cell someone else holds, or through a blocker. Set it only when the story insists; the move is still charged, so the participant has no movement left afterward.

description: Take a character out of the encounter in progress. If they are taking their turn, it ends and the next participant's turn follows.

Adjust the encounter's turn order, or whose turn is running now. Give order as every participant's name in the new sequence, current as the participant whose turn should be open now, or both. Use it only when the rule set's initiative or the story calls for an exception, such as a held or delayed action, choosing a side's order, a surprise round, or correcting a mistake. Choosing a side's order sets the order its members will take; it does not cut a running turn short. Never use it in normal play: the turn order stands, and the player presses End your turn to pass their character's turn. To let another character act now because the player insists, pass force true to that attack instead.

current.description: The participant whose turn should be running now. Leave it out to keep the current turn.

order.description: Every participant's name, in the new turn order. Leave it out to keep the current order.

description: Create an encounter map: a grid of cells set in an existing location, where a tactical encounter takes place. Use it before starting an encounter there. Cells are scaled by the rule set's grid.

ambient.description: An ambient look id from map_options: day, dusk, night, torchlit, foggy, underwater, or magical.

description: Change an encounter map: its name, the location it is in, its size, or its description. Refused if the new name is taken or a participant would be left outside the new size.

background.description: A terrain id for the board's background. Leave out to keep it.

background_color.description: A hex colour for the board's ground. Leave out to keep it.

grid_color.description: A hex colour for the board's grid lines. Leave out to keep it.

description: Delete an encounter map. Refused while an encounter is using it.

Start an encounter on an encounter map. Its location becomes the encounter's location. Only one encounter can be in progress at a time. Add every participant after starting, then settle initiative. Until it is settled, the player character and NPCs are listed in the order they join.
End the encounter in progress. Any turn in progress ends with it.

Create a monster NPC in the world. Give a template to start from a bestiary statblock (see search_monster), and any value you give replaces the template's. A creature named exactly like a statblock uses that statblock unless force is set. Attacks replace the template's attacks when given.

Harm a character from a hazard such as a fall, poison, fire, or a sprung trap, in or out of an encounter. Narrate what hurt them. Use it only for harm that does not come from an attack; an attack's harm goes through attack or player_attack.

Resolve a trap, fall, fire, poison, or other hazard that catches the characters. Name the hazard and its NPC targets; the engine rolls each save and applies the damage and condition to those who fail. Use it whenever the fiction springs a hazard, including during an encounter, and for a trap the party prepared earlier: it is part of the world, and its trigger is honored now rather than waiting for a particular character's turn. A player character caught in the hazard rolls their own save: use the rule set's player-save tool first, then apply what it costs. Never use attack or player_attack for a hazard.

hazard.description: The hazard, such as a hidden pit, deadfall, or burning oil.

save.description: The save stat id, such as save_evasion for a pit or save_physical for poison. Leave it out for a hazard that allows no save.

save_modifier.description: A bonus or penalty to the save, such as an easy pit's +2.

damage.description: Dice such as 1d6 for a ten-foot fall, or a whole number of points. Leave it out for a hazard that only applies a condition.

half_on_save.description: True when a passed save halves the damage instead of avoiding it.

condition.description: A condition id such as prone, applied to those who fail the save.

stat.description: The stat the damage takes. Defaults to the rule set's HP or other outside-harm stat.

cause.description: What hurt them, in a few words. Defaults to the hazard name.

description: Restore lost points of a stat, usually hit points, from a healing spell, art, or item. It never restores more than the character has lost.

amount.description: How many points the healing restores before the cap.

cause.description: What did the healing, such as a spell or art.

stat.description: The stat to restore. Defaults to hp.

description: Bring a character back from critical damage, where they were left unconscious and bleeding out. Use it only for a living character who is not dying; a dying character must be stabilized first. Narrate how they survived, and what it cost them. The harm they took stays as it was.

Resolve several NPC attacks on one character at once, such as several foes attacking the same character or one NPC using several weapons. Each attack rolls its own dice. Every attacker must be taking their turn unless force is true, and each attacker spends its one attack action for the turn, so a later attack action from the same NPC is refused. Use it only when the attackers' turns come up, after the initiative is set. Player characters attack with player_attack, not this tool. On an encounter map, each attack must be within its reach or range with a clear line of sight; move its attacker with place_participant first when it is refused for distance.

attacks.description: The attacks to resolve, one entry per attack.

force.description: Resolve the attacks even though they are not the attackers' turns, or the attackers have already used their attack actions this turn. Set it only when the story needs it: an ambush outside the turn order, or a player who insists for the story's sake.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

description: Have a character try to run from the encounter. Pass safe as true only when the character has a safe way out; if not, the attempt is refused. A passed save takes the character out of the fight. A failed save leaves them in the fight.
Stabilize a dying character, stopping the clock that would kill them, when the story gives them aid: a healer, a rescue, a miracle. Narrate how. Use it only for a character who is dying.

force.description: Set true only when the story requires the aid to work without the rule set's usual check. Normally leave it false.

description: Set a character's armor value. Use it when a character puts on or takes off armor, or when a monster's armor changes.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.

description: Make an NPC's attack against a character. Use it only when the attacker is taking their turn, after the initiative is set; an attack by anyone else is refused unless force is true. The tool resolves the statblock's full attacks per action, and that is the NPC's one attack action for the turn: a second attack action in the same turn is refused unless force is true. Player characters attack with player_attack, not this tool. The engine resolves the attack by the rule set's combat rules and narrates the result. On an encounter map, the attack must be within its melee reach or ranged band, with a clear line of sight; move the attacker with place_participant first when it is refused for distance.

attacker.description: The name of the NPC attacking.

attack.description: The name of one of the attacker's attacks, as the statblock lists it.

target.description: The name of the character being attacked.

nonlethal.description: Strike to subdue rather than kill: a target brought down is unconscious, not dead. Only an unarmed attack or a club or staff may be nonlethal.

force.description: Resolve the attack even though this is not the attacker's turn, or the attacker has already used its attack action this turn. Set it only when the story needs it: an ambush outside the turn order, or a player who insists for the story's sake.

description: Ask the player to roll a player character's attack against a target. Use it when the player says what they attack with, the target is in the encounter, and it is that player character's turn; an attack outside their turn, or after the character has used the turn's attacks, is refused unless force is true. When the player orders a different character to attack, such as another player character or a hireling, and it is not that character's turn, do not call this tool for them: say plainly that they hold until their turn, and resolve the attack when their turn comes. Name the character when the table controls more than one player character or a hireling. On an encounter map, the weapon's reach or range and a clear line of sight are enforced; move the character with place_participant first when the attack is refused for distance.

character.description: The player character or controlled hireling attacking, when it is not the campaign's primary player character.

target.description: The name of the character or NPC being attacked.

weapon.description: The weapon or means of attack, such as 'longsword'. It must be carried, or 'unarmed' for fists.

nonlethal.description: Strike to subdue rather than kill: a target brought down is unconscious, not dead. Only an unarmed attack or a club or staff may be nonlethal.

force.description: Resolve the attack even though it is not the player character's turn, or their attacks for this turn are spent. Set it only when the player insists for the story.

description: Roll a save for a character. The engine rolls the die and compares it to the stat, and records the result. A failure does not defeat the character; apply what the save costs yourself.

name.description: The name of the character or NPC.
